Traupman 261, 331

1īcōn: long o in the nominative (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked: īcon, ŏnis). Greek εἰκών, with omega in the nominative and omicron in the other cases (εἰκόνος), whence the short o of īconis. Traupman 261 prints īcōn, īconis.

īcōn1, īconis f.

noun, third declension

an icon on a screen

Classically the Greek word for an image, which Pliny uses once (Lewis & Short).

See also icon, screen, computer.

SourcesLewis & Short: icon
